name: pcb-p-pack
title: PCB-P PACK BMS

finish._cont_route_why: 11 September 2026: one continuation pass of the router before the stub router when a handful of connections are open (A21's lever of 5 September). cont_route.sh keeps the board only if it improves, so it cannot make one worse; it was declared for A alone because only the A clones carried it, and E and P both ended a route at exactly one open.
finish._cont_route_planes_why: 12 September 2026: the continuation exports its own DSN, and it did so with every plane REMOVED, because finish.sh passed it no plane treatment and routeflow never put one in the finish's environment either. That makes the continuation re-route every plane pin as a wire: on C that is GND on In1, the majority of the board's connections. It is the same treatment the route itself is given in routeflow/<phase>.json, and a test holds the two in agreement.
finish._stitch_prune_why: 12 September 2026, P3, and it is A24's case on a two-layer board. P routed 0 hard and 0 unrouted and check_pcb_p refused it for ONE item of 143: a locked GND via at (93.6, 101.3) whose B.Cu end sits outside the ground fill, because the router ran /PACK_F 0.76 mm past it and the fill retreated by its clearance. Two tracks land on the via and both are on F.Cu, so its B.Cu end connects to nothing. Measured on a copy of the routed board before this was turned on: 1 locked via removed of 124, 0 left alone, hard 0 and unrouted 0 both unchanged, and the gate's one failure gone. It stays judged against the board before it (finish.sh 5b) and reverts if it opens anything. NOT the same via as the one that started this: U1's exposed pad had a single thermal via because escape.py was refusing the other four against the land's own solder-paste apertures, and with that fixed all five of its vias reach the B.Cu fill (appendix 32.151).
finish._return_via_why: 15 September 2026, owner ruling 20:15 CEST (appendix 32.198): a ground via within 1.5 mm of every signal via, fine-pitch escape fans exempt; the finish places them after the last copper-changing stage and the board gate (intent_checks item 4) refuses a board with a signal via left without one.
finish._stub_layers_why: 15 September 2026 (P5): the back side is the ground plane and the pack bands; a closure on B.Cu would cut the pour under a front-side signal, which is the gap rule 1 refuses. The stub router closes on F.Cu only.
finish._via_parallel_why: 18 September 2026 (rule PI-003): after every copper-editing stage and before the ground vias, via_parallel lays parallel barrels beside any via dc_drop's solved mesh puts over IPC-2221's rating for its wall (the fabricator's 18 um plating), joined on every layer the net touches there, DRC-guarded, then re-solves and re-judges. On the committed board: P4 passes PI-003; the stage lays nothing and says so

_phase_why: 12 September 2026: the phase is a fact about the board and it lived as a DEFAULT inside each generator, where gen_pcb_c.py still said C9 while the deliverable is C10, and full.sh set it for one board of six. A board's silk then names a phase `verify_deliverable` refuses, after the route, which is how A24 came to carry A18 on its front silk. `full.sh` exports this unless the caller has already set PHASE. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026, THE DECLARATION IS THE BOARD IN THIS TREE AND NOT THE ROUTE IN FLIGHT. It was set to the in-flight phase on 16 September with the reason that final_gate refuses a folder that is not the declared one, and that is exactly what went wrong: every reader that GATES on this field asks 'is this folder the board', so pointing it at a route that has not landed makes those gates answer about a board that does not exist. Board P proved the cost: its P4 folder holds the board this tree holds, byte for byte (sha256 d79865e7b1aceb95), and it was being read as stale against a declared P5 that was measured, refused and abandoned under decision 28. Board A declared A36, a route that was never cut, while the tree carries A32. The phase in flight belongs to the RUN (`routeflow --phase`, with ROUTEFLOW_PHASE_UNDECLARED=1 for an arm whose board may never be adopted), and it moves into this field in the same commit that brings the board in.
_signal_classes_why: Rule RET-001, 16 September 2026. The return-path rule asks what a net's spectral content deserves, so every signal net needs a class and a reason. A net matched by no entry here is UNKNOWN and is judged at the STRICTEST bar, so an omission costs a failure rather than buying a pass. Patterns are shell globs over the net name without its leading slash, first match wins.

signal_classes.basis: SMBus at 100 kHz, open drain, the edge set by the pull-up and the bus capacitance
the gauge's battery-trip interrupt, an edge into the host
the pack-present pin, a static level pulled through a resistor
the display-request button input, pressed by a person
the push-button input of the gauge, the same
a thermistor divider, a DC level changing with temperature
a cell-voltage sense line through its filter, DC by construction
a cell tap, a DC node of the pack
a shunt sense line through its filter, millivolts of DC
the charge FET gate drive and its return, switched at most once per charge cycle
the discharge FET gate drive and its return, the same
the gauge's own supply after its filter
the protector's switched node between the two FETs, a DC node except at a protection event
the battery sense node through its filter

_gnd_grid_why: MEASURED AND REJECTED for this board, 15 September 2026 (/root/piso4 against /root/piso4g). Four-layer P without the grid routes 0 hard and 0 unrouted of 35 nets in 1.4 minutes; with a 2.1 mm ground-via grid laid before the route the same board ends its rounds at 3 and then 21 unrouted. P is 70 by 44 mm carrying the pack path in wide bands, so a grid of stitch vias takes the room the router needs, and prevention that costs the route is not prevention. The return-via fixer works on P after the route instead. This is a declaration of what was tried, not an omission: a board that declares nothing gets no grid and nobody can tell why.
_annular_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002, DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED. Board P is ordered at 2 oz by owner ruling 7, and the fabricator's capability page states its annular ring rows for 1 oz only (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md, read 16 September 2026). Borrowing the 1 oz number for a 2 oz board would be inventing a limit, and etching a heavier copper takes MORE room rather than less, so the 1 oz figure is not even conservative here. The ring stays unjudged on this board until the fabricator is asked directly, which is a question for the order.
_copper_layers_why: Two layers as built. OWNER DECISION 28 IS OPEN on this: two layers cannot hold the return-path rule and the four-layer arm routes 0 and 0 in 1.4 minutes. If the ruling goes to four, this is the line that changes.
_external_ports_why: Rule TRN-001, 16 September 2026. NOTHING ON BOARD P LEAVES THE ENCLOSURE, and this is the sentence that says so rather than a file nobody wrote. P is the pack's own protection and gauge board and it sits in the case beside the cells: J_CELL is the 4S tap harness to the cell block a few centimetres away, J_TS is the thermistor lead into that same block, J_SMB is the gauge's bus to board E inside the case, and the pack current leaves on W_BP and W_BN, two soldered wire lands to board E's own entry. Every one of those conductors begins and ends inside the sealed case, so the electrostatic and surge argument that TRN-001 is about does not reach them: what reaches them is board E's inlet protection, upstream, which decision 31 covers. If a pack lead is ever brought out to a case connector this declaration is the first thing that has to change.

GND.what: the board's single ground: every return on this board is this net

_grounds_why: 16 September 2026, rule GND-001: either the board has one ground and says so, or every partition is drawn deliberately with its crossing points named and the signals that cross listed. ground_system.py reads the netlist and compares it with this.
critical_k_why: l = t_r / (6 t_pd). ECSS-E-HB-20-07A section 6.1.2.3 works a real case where a 35 mm clock track with a 200 ps edge failed a radiated emission test: that track is ONE rise distance long (t_r / t_pd = 34.5 mm on its microstrip), which is k = 1, and the handbook calls it a textbook radiator. k = 2 is half a known failure and k = 6 is a sixth of it. The number is this project's choice; the handbook is what it was calibrated against, and no standard in this tree states a value for k
_safety_lines_why: The pack board carries no line whose assertion inhibits a hazard: its protection is the pack's own protector and the blade fuse, both of which act without a signal, and nothing on it is inhibited by a conductor from anywhere else.
